extracted.intended_audience: researchers, teachers, and students in humor studies (members of the International Society for Humor Studies)
extracted.subtask_description: A catalog listing psychological/behavioral instruments used in humor research, with authorship, category, year, the constructs each instrument measures, and availability notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 WD Humor Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures six scales for the funniness and aversiveness of 3 types of humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Willibald Ruch. Category: Humor Appreciation Test. Year: 1983. Availability: Instrument available from the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antioch Sense of Humor Inventory (ASHI–Part 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference scales for 10 different humor categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Harvey Mindess, Carolyn Miller, Joy Turek, Amanda Bender, and Suzanne Corbin. Category: Humor Appreciation Test. Year: 1985. Availability: Instrument available from online retailers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor Cognition Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Scales for Joke Knowledge, Joke Reasoning, and Overall Humor Cognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Alan Feingold and Ronald Mazella. Category: Humor Appreciation Test. Year: 1993. Availability: Instrument available from the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPAT Humor Test
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Donald L. Tollefson and Raymond B. Cattell. Category: Humor Appreciation Test. Year: 1963/1966. Availability: Limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coping Humor Scale (CHS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven-item scale for humor-related coping with life stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Rod A. Martin & Herbert M. Lefcourt. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1983. Availability: Instrument available from the authors and the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Rod A. Martin and Patricia Puhlik-Doris. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 2003. Availability: Instrument available from the authors and the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous Behavior Q-Sort Deck (HBQD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains 100 items of humor-related behavior and yields 5 dimensions of humorous style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Kenneth Craik, Martin Lampert, and Arvalea Nelson. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1968/1993. Availability: Instrument and manual available through the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidimensional Sense of Humor Scale (MSHS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four scales for Overall Humor Sense, Humor Appreciation, Creativity, and Coping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: James A. Thorson and Falvey C. Powell. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1993. Availability: Instrument available from the authors and the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of Humor Questionnaire (SHQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores for Metamessage Sensitivity, Liking of Humor, Expressiveness, and Overall Sense of Humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Sven Svebak. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1974. Availability: Instrument available from the authors and the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of Humor Questionnaire 6 (SHQ-6 Revised)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a single sense of humor score (revised version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Sven Svebak. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1996 / Revised 2015. Availability: Instrument available from the authors and the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of Humor Scale (Paul McGhee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures Overall Humor Quotient and 8 subscales of humor-related behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Paul McGhee. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1996. Availability: Instrument available from the Laughter Remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situational Humor Response Questionnaire (SHRQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall score for the tendency to be amused and laugh easily across situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Rod A. Martin & Herbert M. Lefcourt. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1984. Availability: Instrument available from the authors and the ISHS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-Trait-Cheerfulness-Inventory—State Part (STCI-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures state cheerfulness, state seriousness, and state bad mood for 4 time points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Ruch, Köhler, & van Thriel. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1997. Availability: Instrument Available from the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-Trait-Cheerfulness-Inventory—Trait Part (STCI-T)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures trait cheerfulness, trait seriousness, and trait bad mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship: Ruch, Köhler, & van Thriel. Category: Self-Report Scale. Year: 1996. Availability: Instrument available from the authors.
